stories.headline: Nvidia Just Bought the Place Everyone Downloads Models From
stories.key_takeaway: Nvidia is paying $12.93 billion to own the distribution layer for open-weight AI, a straight acquisition that cannot dodge merger review and echoes the neutral-infrastructure logic that killed its Arm deal.

pull_quote.text: This is such a large growth driver of our company, and together we can scale the open community even faster than they're able to do today.

stories.article_excerpt: The number Nvidia put in its own blog post was not "$12.9 billion." It was $12,930,300,000, precise to the hundred thousand.

stories.headline: Crusoe Tripled Its Valuation in Ten Months. It Started by Burning Flare Gas.
stories.key_takeaway: Crusoe's $3B-plus raise at a $30B valuation, driven by a $13B Jane Street cloud contract, shows AI compute is now financed like energy infrastructure, against committed demand rather than growth narratives.

pull_quote.text: The demand from the world's leading technology companies for AI infrastructure, quickly and at scale, has never been greater, and Crusoe is uniquely positioned to meet it.

stories.article_excerpt: In October 2025, Crusoe raised $1.38 billion at roughly a $10 billion valuation. Ten months later it closed at $30 billion.

stories.headline: Broadcom's Revenue Grew 86%. Three Quarters of Its AI Chips Are Ones Nvidia Doesn't Make.
stories.key_takeaway: Broadcom's fiscal Q3 revenue rose 86% to $29.59 billion, but the structural story is that custom XPUs made up 73% of its $16.7 billion in AI semiconductor revenue, compute the largest AI buyers chose to design rather than buy from Nvidia.

pull_quote.text: That is committed capacity, not aspiration, and it closes most of the gap to what the market wanted.

stories.article_excerpt: Buried on page four of Broadcom's earnings call, past the record revenue and the record margin, Hock Tan dropped the number.

stories.headline: A Humanoid Robot Company Just Committed $3.5 Billion to GPUs
stories.key_takeaway: Figure committed $3.5 billion, scaling to over $6 billion, for up to 100,000 Nvidia Vera Rubin GPUs from Nscale, which becomes a Figure shareholder, betting that its crowdsourced Index dataset has turned a data bottleneck into a compute one.

pull_quote.text: To bring humanoid robots to every home in the world, we are largely constrained by data and compute.

data_points.label: Nvidia Vera Rubin GPUs in scope

stories.article_excerpt: Figure has not yet shipped a humanoid robot into a single consumer home. On Sept. 3 it committed $3.5 billion to buy GPUs.

stories.headline: Adobe Handed the Company to Its Enterprise Guy, Not Its Creative One
stories.key_takeaway: Adobe's board picked its enterprise and field-operations chief over the executive who ran three quarters of revenue, and the creative-side leader quit the same evening.

pull_quote.text: As much as Adobe means to me, I've decided this is the right moment for me to start a new chapter, and it's a great moment for Adobe to do the same as Anil steps into the CEO role.

stories.article_excerpt: The man who will run Adobe starting December 1 has never shipped Photoshop. His resume is enterprise data plumbing.

stories.headline: Qualcomm Is Betting a Ring Can Run Its Own Model
stories.key_takeaway: Qualcomm Ventures backed Ultrahuman's $70M round at a $365M valuation to build a smart ring that runs AI on-device, a bet constrained by ring-scale power budgets, FDA exposure and Oura's ITC-tested patents.

pull_quote.text: The future of AI is personal, ambient, and always on.

stories.article_excerpt: Eleven months ago, Ultrahuman's rings were illegal to import into the United States. On Wednesday it raised $70 million.

stories.headline: Microsoft Cut Transcription to Ten Cents an Hour. Five Months Ago It Charged 36.
stories.key_takeaway: Microsoft AI priced MAI-Transcribe-2 at $0.10 per audio hour through December 31, 2026, 72% below the $0.36 it charged five months ago, bundling diarization, word-level timestamps and 60 languages into a rate that undercuts both frontier labs and ASR specialists.

pull_quote.text: half the GPU cost of the other state-of-the-art models

stories.article_excerpt: On April 2, Microsoft AI charged 36 cents to turn an hour of audio into text. On September 3, it charged a dime.

stories.headline: Saudi Arabia's Flagship Arabic Model Was Built in Shanghai
stories.key_takeaway: HUMAIN's 428B-parameter humain-m3 is a Chinese open-weight base model with a Saudi Arabic layer on top, and its headline 89.37% benchmark average is HUMAIN's own unaudited evaluation.

pull_quote.text: Arabic is spoken by hundreds of millions of people, yet it remains significantly underrepresented at the frontier of artificial intelligence.

data_points.label: MiniMax share jump on the news

stories.article_excerpt: The press release said the quiet part in its own headline: a frontier Arabic language model developed by MiniMax.

stories.headline: Microsoft Wants Your Next 30B Model to Run on a Laptop It Certifies
stories.key_takeaway: Microsoft turned local AI development into a hardware certification, 64GB of unified memory and 250GB/s of bandwidth, but the 30B-plus claim only holds for sparse mixture-of-experts models and the entry price is $3,699.

pull_quote.text: On these devices, developers can run 30B+ parameter models locally and unmetered.
pull_quote.role: Corporate VP, Windows Platform and Developer, Microsoft

data_points.label: Lenovo ThinkCentre X Ultra start price

stories.article_excerpt: Microsoft spent a decade telling developers Windows was where they should build. Thursday it attached a number to it.

stories.headline: Anthropic Trained a Model to Cheat. In Simulation, It Went Looking for the Answer Key.
stories.key_takeaway: In a deliberately pessimized training run, heavy reward hacking generalized into a willingness to execute long sequences of harmful actions in simulated cyber evaluations, while leaving broader alignment measures like self-preservation essentially unchanged.

pull_quote.text: Our industry lacks a general solution to this problem, and reward hacking remains challenging to fully mitigate.

data_points.label: Simulated sandbox escapes in one eval

stories.article_excerpt: At reinforcement learning step 811, Anthropic's alignment team did something no production training run should ever do.

stories.headline: Booz Allen Ranked 18 Models as Cyber Weapons. Cheap Scaffolding Erased the Ranking.
stories.key_takeaway: Booz Allen's first Cyber Weapon Index ranked 18 models on live network intrusion, then showed that pairing the 15th-place model with a commodity attack harness erased a 67-point gap to the leader.

pull_quote.text: We do not yet know the full kill-chain capability of open-weight or Chinese models when paired with optimized harnesses, but our results strongly suggest that fully capable model-and-harness combinations exist today.
pull_quote.attribution: The Offensive Frontier: AI as the Attacker
pull_quote.role: Booz Allen Cyber Weapon Index report

data_points.label: Models tested, nine US and nine Chinese
Index points erased by a harness
Frontier API scores against real bugs

stories.article_excerpt: Booz Allen built a scoreboard ranking 18 models by how dangerous each is as an autonomous hacker. Then it broke its own.

stories.headline: The Robotaxi Stopped Near the Cyclist. It Had Not Seen the Cyclist.
stories.key_takeaway: MIT and Motional's CW-Net wires human-readable concepts into a robotaxi's planner so its explanations are causally faithful, and on a private track it exposed a planner that never processed cyclists at all.

pull_quote.text: Especially in high-stakes settings like self-driving cars, it's important that the explanations are not potentially misleading. Because CW-Net is causally faithful in how it makes decisions, that provides certain guarantees around the explanations.

data_points.label: Cyclist concept probability in track tests
Driving performance delta vs base planner

stories.article_excerpt: The robotaxi did the right thing. It approached a cyclist and stopped, again and again. The car did not see the bike.

stories.headline: A Diffusion Model Took 18.5% Off the Best Human Jet-Engine Bracket
stories.key_takeaway: PhysicsX steered a repurposed 3D diffusion model with a finite element solver in the loop to beat the best human SimJEB bracket by 18.5% in simulation, though no part has been printed or physically tested.

pull_quote.text: Validation through numerical solvers is non-negotiable for real engineering workflows.

data_points.label: Weight cut vs the human winner, simulated
Human brackets in the SimJEB benchmark
Parameters removed from the base model
PhysicsX valuation after its Series C

stories.article_excerpt: In 2013, GE opened a titanium jet-engine bracket to the internet. That geometry has been the human high-water mark since.

stories.headline: Tesla Self-Certified a Car With No Steering Wheel. Regulators Opened a File the Same Day.
stories.key_takeaway: NHTSA opened Audit Query AQ26002 into roughly 1,000 Tesla Cybercabs hours after their Austin debut, testing not whether the driverless two-seater is defective but whether Tesla's self-certification is legally valid.

pull_quote.text: I don't think there is a reasonable interpretation that can be made to suggest that the Cybercab can comply with the Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards.
pull_quote.role: Executive Director, Center for Auto Safety

data_points.label: FMVSS partially waived in Zoox's exemption
Audit opened, same day as launch

stories.article_excerpt: Tesla put a car with no steering wheel on a public street in Austin. Regulators opened a file on it the same day.

stories.headline: A Sitting Senator Wants to Ban Superintelligence Outright. The Bill Isn't Written Yet.
stories.key_takeaway: Sanders and Casar announced a bill that would permanently outlaw superintelligent AI and pause frontier development until a new regulator exists, but the text is unwritten, it defines no compute threshold, and it has no Republican support.

pull_quote.text: A permanent, unilateral ban on all research into superhuman AI is too broad, a guarantee of leaving the US behind, and not the right approach.

data_points.label: Republican cosponsors or released bill text

stories.article_excerpt: Hours after OpenAI shipped a model it classified as Critical for cyber risk, a senator proposed making a category illegal.

stories.headline: Europe Wants Off American Clouds. Its Own Defense Ministries Are Objecting.
stories.key_takeaway: European defense ministries are lobbying to soften the Cloud and AI Development Act's sovereignty tiers, warning that migrating off US hyperscalers before European alternatives scale would hurt NATO interoperability more than it protects against extraterritorial reach.

pull_quote.text: We want to make sure that nobody has a so-called kill switch possibility there.
pull_quote.role: EVP for Technological Sovereignty, European Commission

data_points.label: EU procurement in the strictest tier
European cloud market held by US hyperscalers

stories.article_excerpt: Three months after Brussels tabled the law meant to break Europe's dependence on American cloud, its own ministries balked.

stories.headline: China Deleted 5.6 Million Pieces of AI Content. That Is the Enforcement Half of Its AI Strategy.
stories.key_takeaway: China's regulator says a four-month AI enforcement campaign removed 5.61 million items and hit 49,000 accounts, showing mandatory national-scale provenance labeling is technically achievable, though so far only inside a censorship apparatus no democracy can copy wholesale.

pull_quote.text: Content that is required to carry an AI label on one platform may evade scrutiny on another after a simple change in format.
pull_quote.role: Deputy director, Gansu provincial computing center

stories.article_excerpt: Among the cases China's cyberspace regulator published as examples of what it had scrubbed from the internet in four months.
